statement: The function returns a result r. Call a transaction any pair of indices (b, s) with 0 <= b < s < len(prices). Call a valid scheme any sequence of transactions (b_1, s_1), ..., (b_m, s_m) with 0 <= m <= k and s_j < b_{j+1} for every 1 <= j < m. Its profit is the sum over j = 1..m of (prices[s_j] - prices[b_j]); the empty scheme (m = 0) has profit 0. Then r equals the maximum profit over all valid schemes with at most k transactions.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, and 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices).

statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail (no overflow, no out-of-bounds access, no panic) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, and 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= k * (M - m), where M = max { prices[i] : 0 <= i < len(prices) } and m = min { prices[i] : 0 <= i < len(prices) }.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, and 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is at most the sum of max(0, prices[i+1] - prices[i]) over all i with 0 <= i < len(prices)-1.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, and 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every pair of indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(prices), r >= prices[j] - prices[i].
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, and 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices).

statement: If max_profit(k1, prices) returns r1 and max_profit(k2, prices) returns r2, then r1 <= r2.
preconditions: 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, and 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices).

statement: The function returns a result r and r equals the sum of max(0, prices[i+1] - prices[i]) over all i with 0 <= i < len(prices)-1.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices), and 2*k >= len(prices) - 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices), and prices[i] = prices[0] for every i.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = prices[len(prices)-1] - prices[0].
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices), and prices[i] <= prices[i+1] for every 0 <= i < len(prices)-1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a valid scheme with at most k transactions (a sequence of index pairs (b_1, s_1), ..., (b_m, s_m) with 0 <= m <= k and 0 <= b_1 < s_1 < b_2 < s_2 < ... < b_m < s_m < len(prices)) whose profit, sum over j = 1..m of (prices[s_j] - prices[b_j]), equals r.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, and 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices).

statement: If max_profit(k, p) returns r and max_profit(k, q) returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(p) = len(q) <= 1000, 0 <= p[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= q[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(p), and there is an integer c such that q[i] = p[i] + c for every i.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0 if and only if prices[i] >= prices[i+1] for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices)-1; equivalently, no pair i < j has prices[i] < prices[j].
preconditions: 1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, and 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices).

statement: The function returns a result r and r = max({0} union { prices[j] - prices[i] : 0 <= i < j < len(prices) }).
preconditions: k = 1, 1 <= len(prices) <= 1000, and 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(prices).
